newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn, SPD cautious ahead of Tuesday tax summit.
newsitem.headline: Bonn, SPD cautious ahead of Tuesday tax summit.

text.p: German coalition leaders and opposition Social Democrats (SPD) on Tuesday remained cautious about prospects for a breakthrough in crunch tax talks later in the day.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel told Bavarian radio that SPD leader Oskar Lafontaine had already set high hurdles to clear, and would probably raise the stakes due to pressure from within his party.
But Waigel said he still expected to reach a compromise on cutting entry-rate income tax and corporation tax -- elements of a 30 billion mark tax reduction package he has proposed.
Paul Friedhoff, economics spokesman of junior coalition partners the Free Democrats (FDP), said the talks would fail if the SPD did not offer proposals that led to tax reductions.
"If it turns out that no tax cut comes out of the whole operation, then no result will come out of this summit," he said in an interview with InfoRadio.

Chancellor Helmut Kohl was due to meet Lafontaine at 1000 GMT in the federal chancellery in an attempt to reach a breakthrough and clear the way for tax reforms aimed at reviving the economy and reducing near-record unemployment.

The talks were expected to last around three hours. Both sides have said failure to make progress would kill off the negotiating process. The SPD can block most tax measures through its control of the upper house of parliament.

In another radio interview on Tuesday, SPD finance expert Ingrid Matthaeus-Maier said she expected the two sides to agree on an entry-level tax rate, the amount of income allowed before taxes kick in, and cuts in labour costs and corporate taxes.
"But we are at odds on the question of the top income tax rate," she told DeutschlandRadio Berlin.
Bonn has proposed cutting the top income tax rate to 39 percent from 53 percent, and the entry rate to 15 percent from 26 percent. It wanted to tax income above 13,000 marks for single wage-earners.
The SPD wanted a smaller drop in the top tax rate and the tax-free threshold set at 14,000 marks.
The coalition has said that keeping the highest income tax bracket too high would violate the constitution if corporate taxes are reduced sharply.

Taking part in the talks for the coalition will be Kohl, Waigel, Wolfgang Schaeuble, parliamentary leader of Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), FDP leader Wolfgang Gerhardt and FDP parliamentary head Hermann Otto Solms, Michael Glos, parliamentary chief of Waigel's Christian Social Union (CSU) and Chancellery Minister Friedrich Bohl.

Lafontaine will lead the SPD delegation, which includes parliamentary leader Rudolf Scharping, Hamburg mayor Henning Voscherau, Brandenburg state premier Manfred Stolpe, North Rhine-Westphalia finance minister Heinz Schleusser and finance policy spokeswoman Matthaeus-Maier.
